title: European partner choice — recent national statistics
note: Citizenship, birthplace, and migrant-background definitions differ by country. Netherlands and Nordic figures are origin-group endogamy among marrying persons; Germany/Italy/Spain/France/Belgium/Switzerland/Portugal are shares of registered marriages involving a foreign national (or different nationality group).

netherlands.title: Netherlands — marriage partner by origin (2021)
netherlands.source: CBS, Rapportage Integratie en Samenleven 2022 (table published 1 Dec 2022).
netherlands.note: Among people marrying in 2021. ‘Same origin’ combines a co-ethnic partner already in the Netherlands and a migration marriage. Second-generation Turkish and Moroccan newlyweds remain ~80% endogamous; Caribbean and Indonesian origins marry Dutch-background partners far more often.

germany.title: Germany — German × foreign-national marriages
germany.source: Destatis Eheschließungen zwischen Deutschen und Ausländern; BiB Fakt L117.
germany.note: Citizenship at marriage, not ethnicity. BiB summarises roughly 86% both German, ~11% one German / one foreign, ~3% both foreign among registry marriages.

france.title: France — French × foreign-national marriages (INSEE)
france.source: INSEE état civil Retro6 — Mariages selon la nationalité des époux (Français ou étranger), champ France.
france.note: FR_ETR = one French and one foreign citizen (mariage mixte). Shares computed from Retro6 absolute counts across opposite- and same-sex marriages.

italy.title: Italy — mixed-citizenship marriages (2022)
italy.source: ISTAT, Matrimoni, unioni civili, separazioni e divorzi — Anno 2022 (Dec 2023 report).
italy.note: Matrimoni misti = one Italian and one foreign citizen. About three-quarters are Italian husband + foreign wife.

spain.title: Spain — marriages with a foreign spouse (2022)
spain.source: INE Movimiento Natural de la Población / press summaries of 2022 nuptiality.
spain.note: Among opposite-sex marriages, 18.2% had at least one foreign spouse (17.4% in 2021).

belgium.title: Belgium — mixed nationality-group marriages (2024)
belgium.note: Statbel reports 22.5% of marriages between partners from different nationality groups (77.5% same group).

portugal.title: Portugal — Portuguese × foreign-national marriages (INE)
portugal.source: INE indicator 0012711 — Proporção de casamentos celebrados entre indivíduos de nacionalidade portuguesa e nacionalidade estrangeira.
portugal.note: Share of all registered marriages that unite one Portuguese and one foreign national.

switzerland.title: Switzerland — gemischtnationale marriages (BFS)
switzerland.source: BFS su-d-01.06.01.01.17 Heiraten nach Staatsangehörigkeitskategorie der Ehepartner.
switzerland.note: Gemischtnationale Ehe = one Swiss and one foreign national among marriages where the reference person has permanent Swiss residence.

norway.title: Norway — spouse choice among Norwegian-born to immigrant parents
norway.source: Statistics Norway (SSB) register studies of first marriages among Norwegian-born to immigrant parents (birth cohorts 1972–1994; marriages through ~2012).
norway.note: Among those who married: 76% had a spouse with immigrant background; 51% shared parents’ country of origin. Endogamy is higher for Pakistani and Turkish parental origins than for Vietnamese, Indian or Moroccan.

nordicCompare.title: Norway vs Sweden — second-generation partner type
nordicCompare.source: Wiik & Holland, Acta Sociologica (register first marriages 1990–2012, birth cohorts 1972–1989).
nordicCompare.note: Among married second-generation individuals: same-origin partners are far more common in Norway than Sweden; majority-background spouses are more common in Sweden.
